surprises.head: Seattle couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Seattle’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 3.0% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far less than once in a thousand games. You may never see it again.

story.head: The Kraken beat the Mammoth
paras: Jordan Eberle got the scoring started for the Kraken early in the first, but Vincent Trocheck tied it up for Utah on the power play late in the period. Matty Beniers put the Kraken back ahead 2-1 on the power play 26 seconds later. Brandon Montour made it 3-1 on the power play early in the second. The Kraken went 16 minutes without a shot on goal, from late in the second to midway through the third, while the Mammoth put 13 on net. The third period was a wild one. Logan Cooley pulled the Mammoth within one on the power play just 27 seconds into the period. Utah had a goal taken off for offside early in the period. Cooley scored again early in the period to tie it 3-3, but the Mammoth didn’t score again. Seattle had a goal taken off for offside midway through the period, though it didn’t end up costing them. Mackie Samoskevich put the Kraken ahead for good with less than six minutes left, and Frédérick Gaudreau sealed it into the empty net with a minute left.

The Mammoth outshot the Kraken 36-23, but the Kraken’s looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Philipp Grubauer made 33 saves for the Kraken, and Karel Vejmelka stopped 18 of 22 at the other end. The Kraken improved to 7-3-1, third in the Pacific, while the Mammoth fell to 7-4-0, still first in the Central.

items.text: The Kraken won without the better of the chances again. Their record (.650) has been well ahead of what their chances are worth (.458).
All four of the preview’s calls held.
